/-!
# Erdős–Ulam problem

The Erdős–Ulam problem asks whether the Euclidean plane contains a dense set of points
whose pairwise Euclidean distances are all rational numbers. The question was asked by
Ulam in 1946; Ulam and Erdős conjectured that no such set exists. The problem is open.
Tao and Shaffaf observed that the Bombieri–Lang conjecture implies a negative answer, and
Pasten showed that the abc conjecture also implies a negative answer.

The same problem appears as Erdős Problem 212, formalized in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«212»` with the plane modeled as `ℂ`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Ulam_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)
- [Sh18] Shaffaf, J., *A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming
  the Bombieri–Lang conjecture*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 60 (2018), 283–293.
  [arXiv:1501.00159](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00159)
- [SdZ10] Solymosi, J. and de Zeeuw, F., *On a question of Erdős and Ulam*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 43 (2010), 393–401. [arXiv:0806.3095](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3095)
-/

blocks.docstring:
**Erdős–Ulam problem.** Is there a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is dense in the
Euclidean plane and such that the Euclidean distance between any two points of $S$ is a
rational number?

Here "dense" means topologically dense in the whole plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, and the distance
condition is required for every pair of points of $S$ (it holds trivially for a point and
itself, since the distance is $0$).

claims.decomposer_note: A single yes/no question (`answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q)`); 'dense' means topologically dense in the whole Euclidean plane ℝ² (not merely infinite or dense on a curve), 'rational distance' is the Euclidean distance being a rational number (trivially satisfied for p = q), and the conjectured answer (Ulam/Erdős, and conditional on Bombieri–Lang or abc per Tao/Shaffaf/Pasten) is 'no', though the problem remains open so `answer(sorry)` is appropriate; the article's conditional results, circle characterization, and Harborth consequence are background, not questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical proposition `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q)`, which I verified is faithful: ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) so `dist` is the Euclidean L² distance (checked via EuclideanSpace.dist_eq); `Dense S` is topological density in the whole plane (closure = univ; `Dense ∅` is false so no degenerate witness); `¬ Irrational x` unfolds to `x ∈ Set.range Rat.cast`; the all-pairs quantification includes p = q where dist = 0 is rational, and I proved in a scratch file that it is equivalent to the `Set.Pairwise` form used by the existing `Erdos212.erdos_212`; `answer(True)` = such a set exists, `answer(False)` = the conjectured (Ulam/Erdős, conditional on Bombieri–Lang/abc) negative answer; category `research open` is correct since the problem is unconditionally open. c01 chosen for the most complete module docstring/references and AMS `11 52` (matching `ErdosProblems/212.lean` and the 'number theory' tag); my only edits were wrapping its >100-char URL line (as c07 did) and one sentence in the module docstring mentioning the Ulam/Erdős conjecture.

Ulam in 1946; Ulam and Erdős conjectured that no such set exists. The problem is open.
Tao and Shaffaf observed that the Bombieri–Lang conjecture implies a negative answer, and
Pasten showed that the abc conjecture also implies a negative answer.

The same problem appears as Erdős Problem 212, formalized in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«212»` with the plane modeled as `ℂ`.

*References:*

- [Sh18] Shaffaf, J., *A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming

namespace ErdosUlamProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
**Erdős–Ulam problem.** Is there a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is dense in the
Euclidean plane and such that the Euclidean distance between any two points of $S$ is a
rational number?

Here "dense" means topologically dense in the whole plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, and the distance
condition is required for every pair of points of $S$ (it holds trivially for a point and
itself, since the distance is $0$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem erdos_ulam_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q) := by
  sorry

end ErdosUlamProblem

items: The plane is modeled as `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (repo scoped notation from `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean`), so `dist` is the Euclidean (L2) distance, as in the sibling file `Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean`.

'Dense' is formalized as Mathlib's topological `Dense S` for `S : Set ℝ²`, i.e. dense in the whole plane (not merely infinite or dense on a curve). `Dense ∅` is false, so the empty set is not a degenerate witness.

'Rational distance' is formalized as `¬ Irrational (dist p q)`, which unfolds to `dist p q ∈ Set.range Rat.cast`; this matches the idiom in `Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean`. The condition is imposed on all pairs `p, q ∈ S` including `p = q`, where it holds trivially (distance 0), so this is equivalent to the `Set.Pairwise` form.

The question is stated with `answer(sorry)`: `answer(True)` is a positive answer (such a set exists), `answer(False)` the negative (conjectured) one. The problem is open, so `research open` is used and the conditional results (Bombieri–Lang / abc) are only mentioned in the module docstring.

The same problem is already formalized as Erdős Problem 212 in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/212.lean` (with the plane modeled as `ℂ`); this is noted in the module docstring without importing that module, since existing Wikipedia pointer files contain no theorem and the task requires a named `sorry` declaration here.

AMS tags chosen as 11 (Number theory) and 52 (Convex and discrete geometry), matching the tags of `ErdosProblems/212.lean` and the problem's 'number theory' tag; 'arithmetic geometry' concerns only the conditional background results.

A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming the Bombieri–Lang conjecture

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted anything and no decomposition objections were raised. The statement is a Wikipedia-collection duplicate of the existing `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/212.lean` (stated there over ℂ with `Set.Pairwise` and `dist ∈ Set.range Rat.cast`); the final file cross-references it in the module docstring (in the style of `Wikipedia/HadwigerNelson.lean`) but does not import it, since the Wikipedia collection idiom uses `ℝ²` (cf. `RationalDistanceProblem.lean`). A reviewer might prefer to make this a pointer file instead of restating, but the restatement is faithful and provably equivalent. Minor ambiguity: 'dense' could in principle be misread as 'dense on a curve'; the article explicitly means dense in the whole plane, which is what `Dense S` for `S : Set ℝ²` encodes. Compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
